To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
task unrelated thought is reduced when the stimuli used in a task are categorized.
the production of task unrelated thought (Tut) is reduced when a categorical organization is used for a memory task and for a verbal fluency task.
the generation of task unrelated thought is influenced by the stimulus organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of stimulus organization in cognition.
the role of stimulus organization in cognitive processing and consciousness.
the role of distributed processing in the maintenance of task focus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of these three studies are consistent with distributed processing and are inconsistent with the predictions of encapsulated processing.
task unrelated thought (Tut) is not a unitary construct.
task irrelevant thought is a function of the task and not a function of a general resource limitation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the organization of the stimulus set has a profound impact on the ability to maintain task focus.
the organization of the task at hand is a key determinant of task performance and that the generation and maintenance task focus can be explained in distributed models of cognition.
the organization of the stimulus material is important for task focus and that task focus is important for the generation and maintenance task unrelated thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way information is organized in memory can have important effects on cognitive processes.
the organization of information can influence the amount of thought unrelated to the task at hand.
the organization of the stimulus can have a profound effect on cognition.
